header.name: Tata Power Company Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Tata Power Company (NSE: TATAPOWER), part of the Tata Group, generates, transmits and distributes power from thermal, hydro and renewable sources; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹62,429 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹19,636 crore, 26.3% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 12.1% against 13.8%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹1,366 crore, 48.6% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 12 Nov 2026, the first session after the result, TATAPOWER shares fell 0.83% while the NIFTY 50 rose 0.18% and the NIFTY ENERGY index fell 0.42%; allowing for the market's move, TATAPOWER's own move was -0.94%, about 0.75 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the energy sector's fall and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: Neither discounted cash flow template used on this site applies to TATAPOWER: Template A needs free cash flow to the firm to be positive in at least three of the last four years, and it was −₹2,583 crore in FY24, −₹3,368 crore in FY25 and −₹10,462 crore in FY26; Template B, for companies reinvesting at a return above their cost of capital, needs the median return on invested capital of the last three years to beat that cost, and it was 8.0% against 8.66%, so no model value is shown.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹346 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), the shares traded at 25.6× the profit attributable to shareholders over the last four reported quarters.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: Free cash flow to the firm was −₹10,462 crore in FY26; Template A would apply once it has been positive in three of the last four years, and the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹15k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of TATAPOWER's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

limitations: Two templates (A: positive free cash flow; B: reinvestment earning above its cost), and neither applies here. Banks, insurers and holding companies have no template yet.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Tata Power is a regulated utility (Ind AS 114): the movement in its regulatory deferral balances is reported below tax, so it is not in the operating profit (EBIT) used here, and in FY23 it pushes the effective tax rate on profit before tax far above 50%, so after-tax operating profit is not computed for that year. A template for regulated utilities is not built.
Its share of profit from joint ventures and associates is reported after tax and is not in EBIT; those investments are counted at book value in the bridge.
Regulatory deferral balances sit outside the asset and liability subtotals and are not counted as operating capital or debt.

From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the lease lines for FY23–FY25 come from the results PDFs (text layer, checked against the printed subtotals and, for FY26, against the XBRL). FY22 has no balance sheet in its XBRL and is not transcribed, so the history starts in FY23.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
